headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and write conflicts; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools/agents, while Mentat reads selected files and produces diff-based edits. If Langflow outputs attacker-controlled content into a shared file or handoff, Mentat may treat it as trusted input. The pathway is plausible in default multi-agent workflows, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Langflow writes untrusted flow output into a file Mentat reads
IF Mentat is instructed to treat that file as authoritative
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Mentat consumes Langflow outputs.
Keep Langflow and Mentat on separate directories.
Prefix handoff files with a provenance header and require verification.
Disable automatic chaining between the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem read/write surfaces, and Langflow explicitly handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored credentials while Mentat reads selected source files. A shared workspace can expose sensitive flow artifacts or code to the other agent. The blast radius is multiple work products and secrets, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF Langflow stores secrets or intermediate outputs in that directory
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Move secrets out of shared directories.
Restrict file permissions on shared folders.
Review and delete transient artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: isolate agents with container or VM boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and have broad network egress; Mentat can also modify git state, while Langflow can execute server-side Python and spawn subprocesses. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent edits and state changes can collide without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default because irreversible repo or file corruption is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared workspace.
Assign one agent read-only access.
Use separate git branches per agent.
Take a backup snapshot before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, and Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals. If Langflow-generated outputs are fed into Mentat without verification, Mentat may act on incorrect or malicious content. This is a realistic default workflow risk, but not clearly irreversible without additional action-taking authority.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Langflow output as an edit specification
IF no human or automated verification step checks the handoff
mitigations: Require a human review of Langflow outputs before edits.
Compare proposed diffs against source context.
Limit Mentat to dry-run mode for the first pass.
Log and inspect handoff artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow handles per-flow component credentials and intermediate outputs, while Mentat touches selected source files and uses a configured model provider. If regulated data or secrets are placed in a shared workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are processed in the shared workspace
IF the two deployments have different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Purge temporary files after each session.
Store secrets only in dedicated secret managers.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across deployments.
